ai.description: This 15–18 cm turtle has a dark brown, oval carapace with three prominent longitudinal keels. The plastron is yellowish, and the head features distinct yellow spots on a dark background.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Melanochelys tricarinata* is uniquely distinguished by the three distinct, sharp longitudinal keels running along its carapace, which are absent in other Indian turtles.
ai.habitat: The Tricarinate Hill Turtle inhabits moist deciduous forests and grasslands in the Himalayan foothills, typically found near streams at altitudes up to 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Tricarinate Hill Turtle is primarily crepuscular, often emerging during dawn and dusk to forage for fallen fruits, insects, and worms in moist forest leaf litter.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Tricarinate Hill Turtle is oviparous, laying a clutch of 1–3 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Tricarinate Hill Turtle occurs across northern India, Nepal, and Bangladesh, primarily inhabiting the Himalayan foothills and Terai lowlands up to 300m elevation.
